content.text: Med-induced chgs in skin & mucous membranes – most are hypersensitivity rxns
: Ag from foods · insect bites · drugs · enviro · exercise-induced & infect
- "first & fast" - w.in hrs - anaphylactic & atopic responses ← rapid release of vasoactive amines - urticarial drug rxns
(drugs + cytotoxic antibodies cause cell lysis) - rare - IgM & IgG bind Ag on cells · complement activation - ex, Goodpasture syndrome · rheumatic fever
- complement activation → tissue damage - also lupus · RA · Arthus rxn
Serum sickness: primary cause today = meds
genetic incapability to detoxify certain meds
characterized by macules or sm papules after initiation of drug tx
MC occurs 5-14d after initiation of offending med
or w.in 1-2d in previously sensitized individuals
•activates macrophages · eosinophils or neutrophils - diff drugs → diff mechanisms → variable presentation
- for short courses of tx (ex, abx), the eruption may appear
•symmetric - maculopapular - may be confused w viral exanthems → hx & chronology of drug exposure key
•severe: mucous membranes ± constitutional sxs → consider DIHS · SJS · TEN
ddx Kawasaki dz: drug eruption can present w fever + morbilliform rash - conjunctivitis · peripheral extremity erythema · strawberry tongue → Kawasaki instead
bx: interface dermatitis w inflam infiltrate (lymphocytes · neutrophils · eosinophils) - complicated cases can progress to SJS/TEN
resolves after D/C - may persist a few days depending on drug half-life
Self-limited · localized subcut (or submucosal) swelling ← extravasation of fluid into interstitium
Affects mucosal tissues of face · lips · tongue · larynx · hands · ft & genitalia
Onset in min-hrs w spont resolution in hrs-few days
accompanied w other allergic rxn sxs
(urticaria · flushing · pruritis · bronchospasm · stridor · throat tightness · ↓BP)
Bradykinin-mediated (ex, ACEI-induced or hereditary – ← C1 esterase inhibitor deficiency
- ACE inhibitors = BP med class MC assoc w drug-induced angioedema
If there = ⍉info to suggest an external cause & pt has isolated angioedema (w.o pruritis or urticaria) → obtain C4 levels & C1 inhibitor antigenic level
: immediate assessment & ongoing airway protection - epi if severe
Edema of superfic layers of skin ← his-related ↑vasc permeability
aka hives or wheals - intense pruritus · erythematous plaques · occasionally angioedema
: release of vasodilators (his · bradykinin · kallikrein · PGs) form mast cells & basophils of the skin
mast cells & basophils in superfic dermis release his & vasodilatory mediators → pruritus & localized edema - mast cell activation in dermis & subQ tissue → angioedema
eosinophil involvement more common w urticaria ← parasitic infect (Strongyloides · Filaria · Schistosoma · Blastocystis)
*⍉direct role: monocyte IL-6 (activates acute phase reactants · ↑B-cell Ab production) · neutrophil lactoferrin granules (bacteriostatic)
Triggers: foods · meds · heat or cold · stress · insect bites · enviro & infect · idiopathic
circumscribed hives or wheals (blanchable · raised · erythematous areas on skin or mucous membranes)
•transient blanching edematous papules or wheals & plaques (central swelling w surrounding erythema) - itching · burning
•appear & progressively enlarge over min-hrs - may coalesce - ⍉painful but intensely pruritic
•angioedema w urticaria: face · lips · extremities · genitals
Dx: detailed H&P - review recent foods · illnesses · meds · new skin products · travel · insect bites
ask about systemic sxs of anaphylaxis (difficulty breathing · throat/chest tightness · N · abd pain)
labs ⍉generally indicated unless underlying disorder (autoimmune · malig) or urticarial vasculitis suspected
long-lasting painful lesions w residual bruising → urticarial vasculitis → inflam markers · complement · ANA
persistent classic sxs: CBC w diff · UA · ESR · LFTs
allergist referral → skin tests or allergen-specific IgE
- most self-limited (resolve w.in 24h) - tx = short-term relief of pruritus & angioedema
- 1st-line over 1st gen (less sedating · better SE profile · fewer drug interactions · less freq dosing)
) may be added if ⍉response to H1 blockers
glucocorticoids only if prominent angioedema or urticaria persisting beyond a few days
epinephrine auto-injector if any chance of anaphylaxis to triggers - epinephrine for anaphylaxis
Drug rxn w/ Eosinophilia & Systemic Sx (DRESS)/Drug-Induced Hypersensitivity Syndrome (DIHS)
: distinct & potentially life-threatening severe SE characterized by a morbilliform cutaneous eruption w fever · LAD · hematologic abnormalities & multiorgan manifestations
: appears to be mediated by activate of CD4+ & CD8+ T lymphocytes -
most often occurs 2-6wks after med initiation
: fever · pharyngitis · malaise 2-3d b4 rash onset
morbilliform exanthem w accentuation on face · upper trunk · prox extremities
•desquamation develops days-wks after initial eruption - can last several wks
: hepatitis · tubulointerstitial nephritis · pulm sxs (SOB · tachypnea · cough)
exanthema w fever · sus of drug rxn · hsp · LAD · involvement of ≥1 internal organ & hematologic abnormalities
: can show lymphocytosis · atypical lymphocytosis · eosinophilia · thrombocytopenia
: HAV IgM Ab · HBsAg · HBcAb (IgM) · HCV viral RNA
for ⍉response to steroids - plasmapheresis · immunosuppressive drugs other options
